description.value:
Qliph-Scarred. You walked out of a place that should have unmade you. The hollows and fractures in your soul never fully closed, and the world can feel the pressure leaking out.

Qliph-Scarred Traits

  • Creature Type. Humanoid (Qliph-Scarred).

  • Size. You are Medium.

  • Speed. Your walking speed is 6 squares

  • attributes. Your background determines your attribute increases; Qliph-Scarred does not grant any attribute bonuses.

Qliph-Scarred Core. At character creation you gain What Walked Out (Shadow Resilience, Qliphothic Saturation, Hunger Mask, Shadow-Wake). Your heritage adds its own traits and Tier powers at Initiation 1, 5, 11 and 17.

description.value:
“Darkness climbed into your bones and decided to stay.”

Shadow Resilience. Your scars drink in hostile power instead of letting it tear you apart.

  • You have resistance to qliphothic damage.
  • Your presence carries a subtle, unsettling weight; you gain a small bonus to Intimidation checks.
  • The deeper interactions with corruption, Qliphothic zones, and Darkness tracks are handled by Bad Eden engines and GM judgment.

effects.name: Qliph-Scarred: Shadow Resilience
effects.description: You have resistance to necrotic damage and a +1 bonus to Intimidation checks. Any extra “corruption handling” stays narrative/BBTTCC-engine side, not automated rolls.

description.value:
Qliphothic Saturation. The hollows in you are already full of poison light.

  • You have resistance to poison damage.
  • You often sense when a place is spiritually “overclocked” or unsafe; your scars hum in high-corruption zones.
  • Any radiation/corruption hooks in Bad Eden are driven by flags on this feature rather than automatic rolls.

effects.name: Qliph-Scarred: Qliphothic Saturation (Resist Poison)
effects.description: You have resistance to poison damage. Advantage on saves vs the poisoned condition is adjudicated by the GM.

description.value:
Hunger Mask. You learned to wear your appetites like armor.

  • You gain a small bonus to Stealth checks when hiding fear, pain, or desire.
  • Your body handles starvation, deprivation, and toxic cravings slightly better than most (handled narratively).
  • In Qliphothic zones, your mask sometimes slips, revealing the hollow radiance beneath.

effects.name: Qliph-Scarred: Hunger Mask (Social Edge)
effects.description: You gain a +1 bonus to Deception checks when concealing your true intentions or emotional state.

description.value:
Shadow-Wake. Wherever you go, the shadows remember.

  • You leave behind subtle impressions in darkness and ruin; tracking you by mundane means is slightly harder.
  • You gain a small bonus to Stealth checks while in dim light or darkness.
  • Qliphothic entities may recognize the wake you leave, for better or worse (handled narratively).

effects.name: Qliph-Scarred: Shadow-Wake (Stealth Edge)
effects.description: You gain a +1 bonus to Stealth checks, especially when moving through dim light or deeper shadow.

description.value:
“Send the Qliph-Scarred into the bad places. If they come back smiling, it means the rest of probably can still come back.”

Domain Edge. Your Domain leans toward problem-solving in corrupted zones, containment operations, and subtle social pressure.

Corruption-Tuned. You help keep others steady in the presence of Darkness, even when it whispers to you first.

description.value:
“Something fell into you and it’s still awake in there.”

Qliph-Scarred (Diabolic). Your scar is a splinter. Something with a will of its own got into you when you walked out of that place, and you didn’t kick it out so much as you negotiated with it. The tongue in your mouth is not always yours. The advice you give is not always what you meant to say. It is, however, useful.

Traits

  • Creature Type. Humanoid (Qliph-Scarred).

  • Size. Medium.

  • Movement. 6 squares walking.

  • Lineage Lean. Qliph-Scarred does not grant fixed attribute bonuses; your background handles increases. Your heritage leans toward Presence in fiction and through Tier powers.

Qliph-Scarred Core: What Walked Out

Shared across all Qliph-Scarred heritages. Granted at character creation via the base ancestry item.

  • Shadow Resilience. You have resistance to qliphothic damage. You reroll the lowest die on Body checks against effects that would drain, wither, or corrupt your body.

  • Qliphothic Saturation. Once per scene, when you fail a Soul check, you may reroll it — but your scene's Darkness-gain count increases by 1. The scar pays for what the scar saves.

  • Hunger Mask. You can suppress a bodily need (hunger, thirst, sleep, breath) for up to 24 hours by deciding to; you do not suffer its penalties during that window. At the end of the 24 hours, all deferred needs strike you at once, each as a separate Stress-class consequence.

  • Shadow-Wake. Creatures with qliphothic attunement (demons, corrupt sephirot, Radiation-warped entities) can sense you at 12 squares and know you have been marked. They may not know how to read the mark.

Diabolic Traits

  • Splinter Tongue. You know Infernal as a bonus language. You reroll the lowest die on Presence checks to persuade, deceive, or intimidate creatures who are already lying to themselves — the splinter knows its audience.

  • Cold Iron Cost. You take 1 extra point of damage from any weapon forged of cold iron or blessed against fiends. The splinter does not like those things, and you share a body with the splinter.

Domain Edge

  • Domain Edge. Your Domain gains +20 Violence marks at campaign start.

description.value:
"It wasn't your voice. It was a voice you agreed to share."

What's Inside You (1/Soma Break). Action — let the splinter speak. Choose one humanoid you can see within 6 squares who can hear and understand a language you know. They make a Soul check vs. your Resolve.

Failure: they are Calmed by you for 1 minute, or until they take damage or witness you attack them or someone they consider an ally.

Success: they know someone else briefly spoke through your mouth and can describe it to others — they are probably going to tell their friends.

⚔ AURABLADE — MECHANICAL CORE (PHASE 1.5)

Emotion is not flavor text.
Emotion is a resource.

🔥 Burn — What It Is (Plainly)

Burn represents emotional overextension:

  • Adrenaline overload

  • Suppressed fear

  • Moral fixation

  • Spiritual strain

Burn is not a die pool.
Burn is a state track that unlocks power and risk.

You do not “spend” Burn.
You enter Burn states, and the game responds.

🔥 How You Gain Burn (Concrete Triggers)

You gain 1 Burn when any one of the following occurs:

Universal Burn Triggers

  • You hit with an attack granted or enhanced by your Aura

  • You force a defense check using an Aura feature

  • You escalate without pause (GM-flagged high-risk continuation)

  • You remain in the same Aura for too long without stabilizing

⚠️ Limit:
You bank at most 2 Burn a round from landed hits; each Aura action adds 1, and a subclass may say otherwise.

Burn rewards commitment, not spam.

🔥 Burn States (Explicit Bands)

Burn is divided into three states.

🔹 Burn 0–1 — Controlled

You are emotionally steady.

  • You gain only passive Aura benefits

  • No backlash risk

  • No forced effects

This is the safe state.

🔸 Burn 2–3 — Engaged

Your emotion is active and visible.

At this state:

  • Your Aura unlocks standard combat riders

  • Your abilities gain explicit mechanical effects

  • You may choose to push harder

This is the intended combat state.

🔥 Burn 4+ — Overheated

You are exceeding safe emotional limits.

At this state:

  • Aura effects intensify

  • GM is authorized to:

    • Trigger backlash

    • Apply collateral

    • Force Aura collapse on a bad roll or narrative beat

This is the danger state.

🔥 What Happens at Backlash (Clear, Bounded)

When backlash triggers (GM discretion or subclass feature):

One of the following occurs (GM chooses or rolls):

  • You take psychic or sephirotic damage

  • You suffer roll 3d10 keep lowest 2 on your next attack or save

  • Your Aura collapses (you drop to Burn 0)

  • A narrative consequence occurs (fear, escalation, attention)

Aurablades are not punished randomly.
They are punished predictably.

💠 AURA STATES — EXPLICIT MECHANICAL EFFECTS

Each Aura grants:

  • A passive effect

  • Engaged Burn effects

  • Overheated Burn effects

These are not manifestations.
They are combat permissions.

🔥 FURY — Escalation & Force

Theme: Press harder. Break lines.

Passive (Always On)

  • +1 bonus to damage rolls with melee weapon attacks

Burn 2–3 (Engaged)

When you hit with a melee attack:

  • Deal +tier damage

  • You may push the target 1 square or cleave a second creature within reach (once per turn)

You may also:

  • Ignore roll 3d10 keep lowest 2 on one attack per turn

Burn 4+ (Overheated)

When you hit:

  • Target must succeed on a Violence defense or be knocked prone

  • Your attacks deny reactions until the start of your next turn

⚠️ Risk:

  • On a missed attack, GM may trigger backlash

Fury trades control for dominance.

🛡 RESOLVE — Defense & Refusal

Theme: Stand firm. Make removal expensive.

Passive (Always On)

  • +1 bonus to Guard while you have not moved this turn

Burn 2–3 (Engaged)

You may:

  • Halve the next hit you take before the start of your next turn

  • Ignore forced movement up to 2 squares

Additionally:

  • Reaction strikes against you roll 3d10 and keep the lowest 2

Burn 4+ (Overheated)

You may:

  • Automatically succeed on one Violence, Body, or Intrigue check per round

  • Lock your position: enemies cannot move you at all

⚠️ Risk:

  • When damage is fully negated, backlash may occur

Resolve dares the world to try harder.

🤍 MERCY — Protection & Restraint

Theme: Prevent loss. Redirect harm.

Passive (Always On)

  • You may choose to deal nonlethal damage without penalty

Burn 2–3 (Engaged)

Once per round, when an ally within 2 squares takes damage:

  • Reduce that damage by tier

  • You may redirect it to yourself

You may also:

  • Automatically stabilize a creature you touch

Burn 4+ (Overheated)

You may:

  • Prevent an ally from dropping below 1 Integrity (once per round)

  • Convert a failed Last Stand check into a success

⚠️ Risk:

  • Preventing death may trigger backlash or Aura collapse

Mercy delays consequences — it does not erase them.

🕳 DREAD — Suppression & Collapse

Theme: Remove hope. End momentum.

Passive (Always On)

  • Enemies within 1 square suffer roll 3d10 keep lowest 2 on fear and nerve checks (GM adjudication)

Burn 2–3 (Engaged)

On hit:

  • Target must make a Soul defense or be Shaken until the end of its next turn

  • Target cannot take reactions

You may also:

  • Suppress one buff or inspiration effect (GM adjudication)

Burn 4+ (Overheated)

When you hit:

  • Target suffers roll 3d10 keep lowest 2 on all saves until the start of your next turn

  • Nearby enemies must make a defense check or hesitate (lose movement or reactions)

⚠️ Risk:

  • Collateral fear or narrative fallout is likely

Dread does not kill bodies.
It kills belief.

🔄 Changing Aura (Explicit Rule)

You may change your Aura:

  • As a bonus action

  • Or as part of a Soma Break or narrative reset

Changing Aura:

  • Costs 1 Burn

  • Does not clear Burn; Stabilize or Meditate for that

Frequent swapping = control
Deep commitment = power

🧠 How Players Should Think About Aurablade

Ask yourself every turn:

  • “Do I escalate — or stabilize?”

  • “Can I afford another Burn?”

  • “What happens if this goes wrong?”

Aurablades are not forgiving.

They are honest.

The wound is the prayer.

Mode: Martyr

Blood Hymn Aurablades convert suffering into amplification. Where the base class governs Burn and Aura, the Hymn turns each blow into fuel — for cleave, for fear, for irreversible certainty. Played as the operative who runs toward the worst version of the fight on purpose.

Doctrine Features

  • Level 3 — Escalation. Your Burn feeds itself. While at Burn 2–3 (Engaged), weapon attacks deal +tier damage and grant +1 Burn (once per turn). At Burn 4+ (Overheated), the bonus scales further.
  • Level 6 — Lifetithe. Convert flesh into certainty. As part of an attack or Aura effect, take self-damage equal to your tier to gain +1 Burn (no action), reroll one damage die, or reclaim a previously expended Aura effect this turn.
  • Level 10 — Crimson Arc. Your violence spills outward. Once per turn, when you hit at Burn 2+, choose another creature within reach and deal half the original damage to them. At Burn 4+ the secondary target takes full damage and both must check against an additional rider.
  • Level 14 — Terror Charge. Fear trails behind you. While at Burn 3+, creatures you hit make a Soul defense or become Shaken; Shaken creatures suffer 3d10 keep lowest 2 on reaction strikes against you and have reduced movement when fleeing. At Burn 4+ nearby allies of your target are also affected.
  • Level 18 — Final Crescendo (Capstone). Once per Soma Break, as a bonus action: enter Burn 4 immediately. For the rest of the turn, all attacks deal maximum damage and you may cleave freely (no once-per-turn limit). Aftermath: your Burn drops to 0 and you suffer severe backlash.

Anchor Point

The world pushes. You remain.

Rules

⚙ Reroll-lowest on checks and defense checks; the push / pull / prone / Shaken / charm gate is read by the GM.

Level 3 — Escalation

Your Burn feeds itself.

Mechanical Effects

While you are at Burn 2–3 (Engaged):

  • Your weapon attacks deal +tier damage

  • Each hit that gains this bonus adds +1 Burn (once per turn)

While you are at Burn 4+ (Overheated):

  • Your weapon attacks deal +tier additional damage (total +2×tier)

  • Each hit automatically forces a Body check or the target is shaken (roll 3d10 keep lowest 2 on its next attack)

⚠️ Risk

  • Each missed attack at Burn 4+ allows the GM to trigger backlash

Escalation is not optional.
If you hit harder, you burn hotter.

Bound and Bargained

A sealed pact holds itself; you need only keep the terms.

Rules

While your Sealed Pact stance is active, the bindings carry part of your will for you: your Clarity maximum rises by 1.

Requires: Pactkeeper⚙ Applies automatically while the Sealed Pact stance is active: Clarity max +1.

Level 6 — Lifetithe

You convert flesh into certainty.

How This Works

As part of an attack or Aura effect, you may:

  • Take self-damage equal to your tier

  • Choose one:

    • Add +1 Burn without using an action

    • Reroll one damage die

    • Reclaim a previously expended Aura effect this turn

This damage cannot be reduced or redirected.

The blade accepts sacrifice.

Breach Specialist

Everything has a seam. Most people just don’t look.

Rules

You gain a rank in Tinkering. If you already have it, its rank rises by one instead.

When you hit an object, door, barrier, or construct with a weapon attack, you may treat the attack as dealing maximum damage to the target’s objects-only resistances (GM adjudication). Once you do, you can’t do so again until the start of your next turn.

⚙ +1 Tinkering. 🃏 Card — the max-damage-vs-objects rider, once per round.

Level 10 — Crimson Arc

Your violence spills outward.

Mechanical Effects

Once per turn, when you hit a creature while at Burn 2+:

  • Choose another creature within reach

  • Deal half the original attack’s damage to that creature

At Burn 4+:

  • The secondary target takes full damage

  • Both targets must make a defense check or be Shaken until the end of their next turn

Momentum becomes violence.
